root_cause.text: The `__mptcp_retrans` function holds the `msk->fallback_lock` while performing packet reinjection, but the reinjection path can call `__mptcp_try_fallback`, which tries to acquire the same lock again, causing a recursive deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The deadlock trace shows `__mptcp_retrans` holding `fallback_lock` (lock #2) and then `mptcp_sendmsg_frag` calling `__mptcp_try_fallback` which tries to acquire `fallback_lock` again. The patch avoids reinjection when `!msk->allow_subflows` (i.e., infinite fallback is in progress), preventing the recursive lock attempt.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent retransmission when new subflows are disallowed to avoid issues during infinite fallback.
intent_record.what: Added an additional condition (!msk->allow_subflows) to the fallback check in __mptcp_retrans, so that retransmission is also skipped when new subflows are disallowed.
intent_record.how: The condition now triggers the same early exit (release locks, goto clear_scheduled) when either fallback is active or allow_subflows is false, preventing retransmission in both cases.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent retransmission when new subflows are disallowed to avoid issues during infinite fallback.

relevance_review.reason: The change prevents retransmission when new subflows are disallowed, which avoids entering the reinjection path that causes the recursive deadlock described in the root cause.
